facts.statement: Eoneustes is an extinct genus of metriorhynchoid crocodyliform named "dawn swimmer".
facts.quote: Eoneustes (meaning "dawn swimmer") is an extinct genus of metriorhynchoid crocodyliform from Middle Jurassic (late Bajocian to early Bathonian stage) deposits of France.

facts.statement: Eoneustes belonged to the thalattosuchian group, which included species fully adapted to ocean life belonging to the families Teleosauridae and Metriorhynchidae.
facts.quote: Como otras especies de crocodiliformes marinos pertenecía al grupo de los talatosuquios, que incluía especies totalmente adaptadas a la vida en el océano, pertenecientes a las familias de los teleosáuridos y los metriorrínquidos.

facts.statement: Eoneustes does not belong to either of those families but is a basal genus related to Metriorhynchidae and the primitive thalattosuchian Teleidosaurus, grouped in the superfamily Metriorhynchoidea.
facts.quote: No obstante, Eoneustes no pertenece a ninguna de ambas, es un género basal relacionado con los metriorrínquidos y al talatosuquio primitivo Teleidosaurus, que son reunidos en la superfamilia Metriorhynchoidea.

facts.statement: The holotype of E. bathonicus was found in Calvados, Normandy, but was lost during the Second World War.
facts.quote: E. bathonicus: Western Europe (France) of the Middle Jurassic (early Bathonian). It is known from holotype from Calvados of Normandy, that was lost during the Second World War.

facts.statement: E. gaudryi is known from a partial skull holotype (NHM R.3353) found in Côte d’Or, Burgundy, and another partial skull from Alpes-de-Haute-Provence.
facts.quote: E. gaudryi: Western Europe (France) of the Middle Jurassic (late Bajocian to early Bathonian). It is known from the holotype NHM R.3353, a partial skull from Côte d’Or, Burgundy and the referred specimen from which housed at Université Claude Bernard Lyon I, F.S.L. 330210, another partial skull from Alpes-de-Haute-Provence, France.

facts.statement: Eoneustes lived during the Middle Jurassic, specifically from the late Bajocian to early Bathonian stages.
facts.quote: Eoneustes (meaning "dawn swimmer") is an extinct genus of metriorhynchoid crocodyliform from Middle Jurassic (late Bajocian to early Bathonian stage) deposits of France.

facts.statement: Eoneustes lived between 168.2 and 165.3 million years ago during the Bathonian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Bathonian to Bathonian (168.2 to 165.3 million years ago)

facts.statement: Eoneustes is classified within the unranked order Mesoeucrocodylia.
Eoneustes belongs to the superfamily Metriorhynchoidea.
The genus Eoneustes was described by Young et al. in 2010.
The species E. bathonicus was originally described by Mercier in 1933 as Metriorhynchus, and E. gaudryi was originally described by Collot in 1905 as Teleidosaurus.
facts.quote: subdivision: E. bathonicus (Mercier, 1933 [originally Metriorhynchus]) E. gaudryi (Collot, 1905 [originally Teleidosaurus]) (type)

rejected.statement: Eoneustes was a carnivore that lived in the oceans and spent most or all of its life at sea.
rejected.quote: Eoneustes was a carnivore that lived in the oceans and spent much, if not all, its life out at sea.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'carnivore that lived in the oceans and spent'
